title: "Part 1 – Credibility as a software problem"
---
::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" icon=false}
**Slides.** [Open the deck at this part](../../slides/one-day-tools.html#/part-1-credibility-as-a-software-problem){target="_blank"} in its own tab, or follow it on the [slides page](slides.qmd).
:::

Part 1 asks what a claim in social science is for and why people describe the field as being in crisis, and then puts numbers on it from the three SCORE studies. It ends inside the one of those studies the facilitator took part in, on five analysts of the same claim who disagreed but whose work could be checked afterwards, because every one of them shipped a readable, runnable document. That is the case for the toolchain, and the next part walks it.

| Work through | What you do | Timing |
|---|---|---|
| Slides, the credibility talk | What a claim is for; the three arguments that made people nervous; why the worry is structural rather than a matter of fraud; the twenty-nine teams of the red-card study; why 'replication' names three different operations; what open research proposes. | 26 minutes |
| Slides, SCORE and its three studies | The programme; reproducibility, robustness and replicability each put to a hundred or more papers; why the three verdicts do not travel together. | 20 minutes |
| Slides, Multi100 from the inside | What an analyst was sent, the paper in one slide, the two tasks and how a hundred studies become one number; then the five-analyst forest, one row at a time, and its software column. What open source buys you. | 18 minutes |
| Slides, what we use today | The workspace, the report and the browser lab in one slide, and what the tools cannot do. | 8 minutes |
| Your workspace, or [Browser lab](../../exercise/browser-lab.qmd) Task 1 | Get to the point where a line of R runs and the panel of 270 country-years is in front of you. | 8 minutes, and the 30-minute break after it if you need more |

**By the end of the part** you have R running with the panel loaded, you can distinguish the three operations that go under the word 'replication', and you can say why five careful analysts of one claim returned five different numbers without any of them being careless.
